behavior: AC1: a stopped or unhealthy gateway fails the local health contract and the two-minute watcher emits one deduplicated incident through kubelab-notify@ after boot grace.
verification: poetry run pytest -q tests/test_hermes_liveness.py -k 'healthcheck or notification_hooks or timer_interval'
evidence: Clean live stop at 21:22:43Z produced unhealthy, successful notifier and one ops-log incident at 21:22:47.606959Z; restart produced recovery after exactly 1 failed run at 21:23:44.059549Z.

behavior: AC2: healthy succeeds; starting, unhealthy, missing and Docker errors fail closed; recovery uses kubelab-notify-recovered@ and ignores provider readiness.
verification: poetry run pytest -q tests/test_hermes_liveness.py -k 'probe or recovery or simple_health'
evidence: 19 focused tests passed: only healthy succeeds; starting/unhealthy/missing/Docker failures fail closed; invalid names exit 64 before Docker; recovery hook is rendered; simple health excludes provider readiness.

behavior: AC3: a powered-off ace2 cannot page because there is no external monitor, persistent timer or always-on dependency.
verification: poetry run pytest -q tests/test_hermes_liveness.py -k 'on_demand or boot_grace or external_monitor'
evidence: Tests prove no Persistent/OnCalendar directive, Kuma monitor or egress dependency; ten-minute local boot grace and two-minute cadence are rendered. Power-off was not physically exercised; no external notification path exists.

behavior: AC4: disabling Hermes disables and removes the watcher; enabling it starts the watcher only after gateway health verification.
verification: poetry run pytest -q tests/test_hermes_liveness.py -k 'unconfigured or activation_order'
evidence: Role tests pin unconfigured teardown (including the probe script) before Compose shutdown, and timer activation after unit installation plus API/Slack/Docker health. A predicted recreation pauses an existing timer without disabling it; unchanged runs do not stop it. All 26 playbooks parse; dry-run contracts pass.

behavior: AC5: provisioning is idempotent, regression tests protect the wiring, and an approved live stop/start records alert and recovery evidence without credentials.
verification: poetry run pytest -q tests/test_hermes_liveness.py && make lint-ansible
evidence: Final suite 10630 passed/96 skipped; Ruff, mypy and 26 playbooks green. Initial pair ended changed=0 and final corrected-head provision changed=0/failed=0. Review-fix recreate measured changed=4 then changed=0 with zero new watchdog messages. Clean drill produced one incident and recovery after 1 failed run; final gateway healthy, timer active, spool 0.
